title: Grindstone Farm
about: Richard “Dick” de Graff started Grindstone Farm in 1981 as a part-time venture on land outside Pulaski, midway between Syracuse and Watertown. In 1988 it became one of the first handful of farms in New York certified organic by NOFA-NY, and a year later Dick left construction work to farm full time. Today he and his wife, Vic, run the farm with Anna Joy Corson as lead gardener, and they have now farmed here for 45 years, 38 of them certified organic.

On about 30 to 40 acres of a roughly 230-acre property, they grow more than 120 varieties of organic vegetables, berries, culinary herbs and tree fruit, with blueberries as the signature crop from late June into September, alongside asparagus, onions, squash, beets and greens. Everything is grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers, with an eye to protecting the soil and the watershed.

Grindstone sells through its CSA and online ordering, an on-farm store open Fridays from spring through December, and farmers markets across Central New York, including the CNY Regional Market. The farm has also trained a generation of young organic growers through its internship and mentorship programs.
facts: Organic vegetables, berries, herbs, tree fruit
